draft.title: Parabolas and hyperbolas
card: Parabola

A parabola is the locus of points the same distance from a point (the focus) and a line (the directrix). With vertex at the origin and focus (0, p), the directrix is y = −p and the equation is x² = 4py.
Hyperbola
The hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 has two branches opening left and right, with vertices (±a, 0). If the y² term comes first, the branches open up and down instead.
Asymptotes
The branches of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 get closer and closer to the lines y = ±(b/a)x without touching them. These lines are the asymptotes.
Example: x² = 20y has 4p = 20, so p = 5 and the focus is (0, 5). For x²/4 − y²/25 = 1, a = 2 and b = 5, so the asymptotes are y = ±(5/2)x.
draft.remember: A parabola is equally far from focus and directrix. A hyperbola follows its asymptotes.

a.q: What are the asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1?
a.why: Here a² = 16 and b² = 9, so a = 4 and b = 3. The asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x = ±(3/4)x. Using 4/3 turns the fraction upside down.
a.clue: Take square roots first, then use b over a.

b.q: What is the focus of the parabola x² = 8y?
b.why: Compare x² = 8y with x² = 4py. Then 4p = 8, so p = 2 and the focus is (0, 2). The answer (0, 4) uses p = 8 ÷ 2 instead of 8 ÷ 4.
b.clue: Match 8 with 4p, then put p on the y-axis.

problems.detail: "If the y² term comes first, the branches open up and down" is loose: what matters is which squared term is positive (as in y²/a² − x²/b² = 1), not the order the terms are written in.

check.summary: The facts, the worked example and both questions are correct, with one clear answer each. The only issue is the card's loose wording that a hyperbola opens up and down when the y² term "comes first"; it should say when the y² term is the positive one.

final.title: Parabolas and hyperbolas
card: Parabola

A parabola is the locus of points the same distance from a point (the focus) and a line (the directrix). With vertex at the origin and focus \((0, p)\), the directrix is \(y = -p\) and the equation is \(x^{2} = 4py\).
Hyperbola

The hyperbola \(\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1\) has two branches opening left and right, with vertices \((\pm a, 0)\). If the \(y^{2}\) term is the positive one, as in \(\frac{y^{2}}{a^{2}} - \frac{x^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1\), the branches open up and down instead.
Asymptotes
The branches of \(\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1\) get closer and closer to the lines \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) without touching them. These lines are the asymptotes.

Example: \(x^{2} = 20y\) has \(4p = 20\), so \(p = 5\) and the focus is \((0, 5)\). For \(\frac{x^{2}}{4} - \frac{y^{2}}{25} = 1\), \(a = 2\) and \(b = 5\), so the asymptotes are \(y = \pm\frac{5}{2}x\).
final.remember: A parabola is equally far from focus and directrix. A hyperbola follows its asymptotes.

a.q: What are the asymptotes of the hyperbola \(\frac{x^{2}}{16} - \frac{y^{2}}{9} = 1\)?
a.why: Here \(a^{2} = 16\) and \(b^{2} = 9\), so \(a = 4\) and \(b = 3\). The asymptotes are \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x = \pm\frac{3}{4}x\). Using \(\frac{4}{3}\) turns the fraction upside down.
a.clue: Take square roots first, then use \(b\) over \(a\).

b.q: What is the focus of the parabola \(x^{2} = 8y\)?
b.why: Compare \(x^{2} = 8y\) with \(x^{2} = 4py\). Then \(4p = 8\), so \(p = 2\) and the focus is \((0, 2)\). The answer \((0, 4)\) uses \(p = 8 \div 2\) instead of \(8 \div 4\).
b.clue: Match 8 with \(4p\), then put \(p\) on the y-axis.
